name: Mill Reach
schools: Gablefen Elementary, a ten-minute walk along Fenwater Walk
walk: The river path, the old mill bridge, and a two-block walk to Courthouse Square.
summary: Workers' cottages and a few loft conversions in the old brick mill, along the Fenwater.
body:
Mill Reach is the oldest built part of town: the 1884 woolen mill, the race, and the short streets of cottages that once housed the second shift.

A handful of the mill floors were divided into lofts in the 1990s. The rest of the Reach is still one-family cottages, close together, with small yards that back onto the water or the alley.

name: West Common
schools: Gablefen Elementary and the middle school on Orchard End
walk: A grid of tree streets; most errands are a bicycle ride or a short drive to the Square.
summary: Foursquares and later farmhouses on a regular grid west of the square, under a stand of old maples.
body:
West Common was platted in 1912, when the mill added a third shift and the town jumped the old corporation line.

The streets are numbered on one axis and named for trees on the other. Lots are deeper than they are wide, which is why so many of the foursquares still have a garage at the alley and a garden between.

name: Ridge Lane
schools: The high school is on the far side of the ridge; a bus runs from Pinion Street.
walk: Steeper streets, wider lots, and a view back over the mill roof to the river.
summary: Later houses on the rise: capes, a few mid-century ranches, and the town's longer views.
body:
Ridge Lane is a single road that climbs the shoulder of the hill, with short courts running off it.

Houses here are later than the Common, and the lots are bigger. On a clear day you can see the mill clock from the upper porches.

name: Ferry Green
schools: Gablefen Elementary, across the old ferry footbridge.
walk: The Green itself, the river path, and a longer walk into the Square along Fenwater Walk.
summary: Bungalows and small capes around the green at the old ferry landing.
body:
Before the mill bridge was built, the ferry crossed here. The green is what remains of the landing, and the streets around it were filled in with bungalows in the 1920s.

It is the quietest of the five neighborhoods, and the one closest to the water after Mill Reach.

name: Courthouse Square
schools: A three-block walk to the elementary school on Orchard End.
walk: Everything is on foot: the office, the library, the bakery, and the bus to the county seat.
summary: The in-town square: brick townhouses, shop fronts with flats above, and the brokerage's own window.
body:
Courthouse Square is two blocks of brick around the 1891 courthouse lawn. The ground floors are still shops; a few of the upper floors are flats, and a short row of townhouses faces the east side.

Gablefen Realty's office is at 12 Courthouse Square, in the bay window that used to belong to a cloth merchant.
